record.context_brief: Dowker complexes and ε-nets on metric graphs
record.original_question: Let G=(V,E,ω) be a weighted simple graph, let d_G be the geodesic distance on V induced by G, and let ε>0. A subset L⊂V is an ε-net if (i) every vertex v∈V lies within distance ε of some landmark u∈L and (ii) every two distinct landmarks u_i,u_j∈L satisfy d_G(u_i,u_j)>ε. Determine optimal upper and lower bounds for the number of elements of an ε-net for G.

evidence.quote: Definition 1.5 (-net). Let (V, dG) be the finite metric space obtained from the weighted graph G = (V, E, ω). Given L = {u1, u2, . . . , ul} ⊂ V and  ≥ 0 then: (i) The set L is an -sample of G if ... for any v ∈ V there exists uj ∈ L such that dG(v, uj ) ≤ . (ii) L is -sparse if for any two distinct points ui, uj ∈ L, their distance dG(ui, uj ) > . (iii) The set L is an -net of G if it is an -sample of G and is -sparse.
Open Problem 1.1. Given a weighted simple graph G = (V, E, ω) and  > 0, determine optimal upper and lower bounds for the number of elements of an -net for G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E, \omega)$ be a finite weighted simple graph, where $\omega : E \to (0, \infty)$ assigns a positive weight to each edge. For $u, v \in V$, let $d_G(u, v)$ denote the geodesic distance, i.e., the minimum over all paths from $u$ to $v$ of the sum of the weights of the edges in the path (with $d_G(v, v) = 0$). Fix $\varepsilon > 0$. A subset $L \subseteq V$ is called an $\varepsilon$-net of $G$ if:
(i) ($\varepsilon$-sample) for every $v \in V$, there exists $u \in L$ with $d_G(v, u) \le \varepsilon$;
(ii) ($\varepsilon$-sparse) for every pair of distinct $u_i, u_j \in L$, $d_G(u_i, u_j) > \varepsilon$.

Determine optimal upper and lower bounds, in terms of $G$ and $\varepsilon$, for the cardinality $|L|$ of an $\varepsilon$-net of $G$. That is, find the tight worst-case maximum and minimum possible sizes of an $\varepsilon$-net for a weighted simple graph with given combinatorial/metric parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 compilation of open problems in applied combinatorics. A web search did not surface any subsequent work providing optimal upper and lower bounds for the cardinality of an ε-net on a weighted simple graph, so the problem appears to remain open.
